newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Eramet board member resigns over sacking.
newsitem.headline: Eramet board member resigns over sacking.

text.p: Swede Stig Ramel said on Friday he would resign from the board of mining company Eramet in protest at the French government's decision to replace the group's chairman.
"The French government are interested in running the company in a way I thought was unacceptable," Ramel told Reuters.

State holding group ERAP said on Wednesday that it would replace the chairman of the French mining company Eramet, Yves Rambaud, on May 29 with Thierry Chambolle and would name three other members to the board of directors.

"The government has forced the chief executive to leave. Mr Rambaud has the confidence of the board and of those working in the company. I thought he was the best person to run the company. That is why I resigned," said Ramel.

ERAP (Enterprise de Recherches et d'Activites Petrolieres) has a 55 percent stake in Eramet and its chairman, Remy Chardon, has criticised Rambaud's handling of a politically sensitive issue involving a nickel mine in New Caledonia.
The French government, which owns ERAP, has launched a procedure to revoke a nickel mining licence held by Eramet in order to award the mine to a group of local Kanak interests.
Canada's Falconbridge is linked with the Kanak Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP).
"(That issue) is the background to the conflict between the leadership and the company," Ramel added.

"Eramet was privatised and international capital was asked to invest in Eramet. We have to draw the line between private and state business and that was not the point of view of the French government," he said.
